title: Abstention, coverage and decision costs
outcome: Choose and evaluate an abstention policy with explicit costs, coverage and held-out evidence instead of reporting only conditional accuracy.

exercises.title: Answer everything
exercises.task: Use threshold 0 on the development fixture.
exercises.hint: Two of four answers are wrong.
exercises.answer: The policy pays 5 twice and averages over all four eligible requests.

exercises.title: Abstain on everything
exercises.task: Choose a threshold above every score.
exercises.expected: Coverage 0, missing conditional accuracy and cost 0.4.
exercises.hint: An empty answered set is not perfect accuracy.
exercises.answer: The operational cost remains defined because every eligible request incurs the abstention cost.

exercises.title: Check equality
exercises.answer: Boundary behavior matters for reproducibility and should be written into the policy contract.

exercises.title: Derive the probability cutoff
exercises.task: Use wrong-answer cost 5 and abstention cost 0.4.
exercises.answer: The derivation assumes calibrated correctness probabilities and zero cost for correct answers. It does not justify using 0.92 on an arbitrary score.

exercises.title: Inspect subgroup coverage
exercises.task: Compute the policy separately for routine and rare requests.
exercises.expected: Report each eligible count, coverage and cost.
exercises.hint: Overall utility can hide service allocation.
exercises.answer: Differences can reflect calibration, difficulty or selection. Preserve group definitions and uncertainty before attributing them to a model mechanism.

exercises.title: Protect the final set
exercises.task: The held-out case exposes a bad threshold. What follows?
exercises.expected: Use it as a diagnosis and collect a new final assessment after changes.
exercises.hint: Changing the policy consumes the old holdout.
exercises.answer: A test failure can guide development, but the same labels cannot remain untouched evidence for the modified policy.
